Cautiously positive. The Committee hiked the federal funds rate and signaled gradual normalization while emphasizing a symmetric 2 percent inflation objective and close monitoring of below-target inflation. This mix of steady tightening and caution is consistent with the literature that stresses anchoring expectations to the target (Woodford; Svensson) and the weak pass-through from a tight labor market to inflation in a flat New Keynesian Phillips curve (Galí, Gertler, López-Salido). By reaffirming its target and gradualism, the Fed mitigates inflation-bias concerns from discretionary policy (Barro-Gordon; Rogoff) and avoids a repeat of the 1970s failure to respond decisively (Volcker-era lessons). The plan for gradual balance sheet normalization reflects awareness of financial/portfolio frictions (Bernanke) and supports a measured approach. Net tone: moderately constructive on growth and employment, tempered by undershooting inflation and low market-based inflation compensation. Adjusting for these literature-based considerations, the sentiment skews slightly less upbeat than a pure read of the hike would suggest.
